candidates.tagline: The phone with a dancing titanium robot arm that winks at you
candidates.story: HONOR launched the Robot Phone on August 12, 2026 — a $1,485 smartphone with a 4-degree-of-freedom titanium robotic arm camera that extends above the screen, tracks subjects, responds to 10 gestures, and dances to music — co-engineered with cinema camera company ARRI, because apparently normal cameras weren't cinematically ambitious enough.
candidates.why_funny: The design brief was apparently 'what if the camera was alive?' and the answer was a phone that can nod its tiny titanium head in agreement with you.
candidates.alt: Side-by-side product photo of the HONOR Robot Phone: left panel shows the silver handset back with its mechanical gimbal arm module; right panel shows a close-up of the robotic camera arm fully extended with the square camera module dangling on the articulated titanium arm

candidates.tagline: The AI data center that drifts across the ocean in a giant sphere
candidates.story: Korean tech giant Naver invested in Panthalassa on August 13, 2026 — a startup building unmanned AI data centers inside wave-powered spherical platforms that drift freely in the open Pacific with no anchors or cables, beaming compute results back via Starlink satellite, because apparently on-land data centres weren't experimental enough.
candidates.why_funny: The CEO describes the floating AI servers as 'like a little Roomba, except enormous' — and if the sphere breaks down in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, good luck dispatching a technician.
candidates.alt: Left: aerial concept render of an Ocean-3 wave-energy platform floating on dark open-ocean water. Right: real photo of the Panthalassa Ocean-2 prototype at sea — a large white sphere with measurement markings, the Panthalassa logo, and an American flag, bobbing in choppy waves
